title: They looked blessed.
paragraphs:
They looked blessed.
He felt betrayed.
That is Psalm 73.

Asaph looked at the wicked and felt envy rising in his chest. They seemed unbothered. Comfortable. Strong. Winning. No fear of God. No visible judgment. Meanwhile, he was trying to stay clean before the Lord and it felt like purity was costing him pain.
That is the ache nobody likes to confess.

Not lust.
Not anger.
Envy.
The kind that whispers, “What’s the point of obeying God if rebels seem to prosper?”
Psalm 73 does not hide that struggle. It drags it into the light. Asaph says his feet had “almost slipped.” Why? Because he started measuring God’s faithfulness by the success of godless people.
And that is where the soul gets dizzy.

But here’s what we miss: the turning point did not happen when the wicked changed. It happened when Asaph entered the presence of God. In worship, his vision cleared. He saw their end. He saw his own heart. He saw that temporary ease is not eternal security.
Then grace walks in.
Asaph realized that God had not abandoned him. God was holding him the whole time. Even in confusion. Even in bitterness. Even in almost-backsliding. The Lord did not let go.
That is the Gospel-shaped hope inside Psalm 73.

Because we all envy something. Beauty. Money. Influence. Pleasure. Ease. We look sideways and start grieving what others have. But envy is never healed by getting more. It is healed by getting near to God.

And we do not come near by our own goodness. We come near through Jesus Christ alone. He is the righteous One who was truly afflicted, truly rejected, truly crushed — not for His sin, but for ours. At the cross, Christ took our wandering hearts and opened the way back to the Father. So now the believer can say with trembling joy: Whom have I in heaven but You? Not because life is easy, but because Christ is enough.
Psalm 73 ends where every restless heart must end:
God is my portion.

Not applause.
Not comparison.
Not the life I envied.
God.
So if envy has been eating your peace, bring it to Jesus. Name it. Repent of it. Lay down the scoreboard. The wicked may shine for a moment, but only Christ satisfies forever.

Your soul does not need their life.
It needs the Lord.
